title: The Operational Facilitator's alignment finding is a pre-vote veto — a misaligned proposal never reaches token holders
content:
A.6.1.1.8.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3 requires the Operational Facilitator to review each Root Edit Proposal "for alignment" within seven days, announcing the finding on the Forum post either way — and where misaligned, to "provide the reasoning for it."

A.6.1.1.8.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 supplies the consequence: "Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Launch Agent 7 Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll." The poll is conditional on the finding. No alignment finding, no vote.

This is the sharpest authority claim in Launch Agent 7's governance: token holders are sovereign only over proposals that have already passed an external alignment screen. The Facilitator cannot enact a change alone, but can unilaterally prevent one from being considered — an asymmetric power that is much easier to exercise quietly than an affirmative one.

The only stated check is procedural transparency: the finding and its reasoning must be posted publicly. There is no appeal route, no override threshold, and no time limit after which an unreviewed proposal proceeds by default. The Artifact relies on reputational accountability of a role defined in another Agent's document (Ozone) rather than on a structural remedy.

The defensible reading is that this is Alignment Artifact Strength applied to Agent governance: the screen exists precisely so that a poorly aligned token-holder majority cannot walk the Agent outside the Atlas. The cost is a single point of governance failure.
description: Only a finding of alignment triggers the Snapshot poll, so a single external role can end a proposal before any vote, subject only to a duty to publish its reasoning.
